title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page 5 of the 'ateliers' section (Chapter IX/IX bis, July 1986). An atelier $\mathcal{A}$ is a set of 'pieces' carrying three relations.
- $X \trianglelefteq Y$ reads like an inclusion or subordination.
- $X \overset{\circ}{\ll} Y$ reads like 'X lies well inside Y', in the sense of contained in the interior.
- $X |\circ| Y$ reads like 'X and Y have disjoint interiors'.

Grothendieck gives a provisional, purely algebraic definition of a homomorphism $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$. It is a map $f:\mathcal A\to\hat{\mathcal A}':=\mathcal A'\amalg\{\emptyset\}$, which embeds in $\mathcal F(\mathcal A')$. In other words it is a partial map, encoded as a map into the pointed set obtained by adding a 'null piece'. It must preserve all three relations: (a) $\trianglelefteq$, (b) $\overset{\circ}{\ll}$, (c) $|\circ|$.

To make sense of this, he extends the relations to $\hat{\mathcal A}'$ by conventions for $\emptyset$, modelled on 'example 2°' of the previous page. That example concerns maps $E\to E'$ and correspondences $\Gamma\to E'$; there pieces mapped outside the target become $\emptyset$.
- (a) $X'\trianglelefteq\emptyset$ and $\emptyset\trianglelefteq X'$ are always true. He therefore notes that $\trianglelefteq$ on $\hat{\mathcal A}'$ is not an order relation.
- (b) $\emptyset\overset{\circ}{\ll}X'$ always holds, while $X'\overset{\circ}{\ll}\emptyset$ holds only if $X'=\emptyset$. So $\overset{\circ}{\ll}$ stays an order with $\emptyset$ as least element.
- (c), completed on the next page: $X'|\circ|\emptyset$ always holds.

The purpose is to set up kernels and quotients. The next page defines $\mathrm{Ker} f=f^{-1}(\emptyset)$. Condition (b) forces the kernel to be downward closed for $\overset{\circ}{\ll}$. He then asks whether every such subset $N$ is a kernel, with a canonical quotient atelier $\mathcal A/N$.

A margin note says that condition c) as stated in Chapter VIII p. 27 does not quite fit, presumably with these conventions.
errors: The convention 'X' ⊴ ∅ and ∅ ⊴ X' always' does more than break antisymmetry, which is what the NB remarks. It also breaks transitivity: X' ⊴ ∅ ⊴ Y' would give X' ⊴ Y' for all X', Y'. So ⊴ on Â' is not even a preorder, and the extended relation can only be used pointwise in condition (a), not composed. This is harmless for the definition itself, which only requires (a) when f(X), f(Y) are not both in A'. It makes (a) vacuous whenever either side maps to ∅.
The definition is explicitly provisional. The marginal note signals an incompatibility with condition c) of an earlier axiom list (VIII p.27), so the axiomatics are not stabilized on this page.

ideas.what: Homomorphisms of ateliers as partial maps, encoded as maps into the pointed object A' ⊔ {∅}, preserving three relations (subordination, 'well-inside', interior-disjointness)
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms of relational structures as partial maps / pointed-set morphisms. Closest are morphisms of contact or proximity algebras (mereotopology).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Partial maps via pointed sets: folklore. Contact/proximity algebras: Efremovich (proximity), de Vries (1962). Region connection calculus: Randell–Cui–Cohn (1992). Contact algebras: Düntsch–Vakarelov and others (2000s).
ideas.where_published: The 'ateliers' notes (1986) are unpublished. Unsure whether ateliers are mentioned elsewhere.

ideas.what: Extension of the three relations to a null element ∅ so that ⊴ becomes trivially true, ≪̊ stays an order with ∅ minimal, and |∘| is trivially true
ideas.modern_name: Adjoining a zero/bottom element to a relational structure

ideas.what: Kernel f^{-1}(∅), forced by (b) to be ≪̊-downward closed, and the question of quotient ateliers A/N (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Kernels and quotients of partial homomorphisms. Analogous to ideals and quotients in contact algebras / Boolean algebras.

missed.claim: The three relations of an atelier (parthood ⊴, 'well inside' ≪̊, interior-disjointness |∘|) are essentially the primitive relations of point-free topology / mereotopology. These are the 'non-tangential proper part' and 'external connection / no overlap' relations of the region connection calculus and of contact algebras. Grothendieck's 1986 attempt to axiomatize pieces of (tame) spaces combinatorially, with morphisms as partial maps and kernels/quotients, parallels contact-algebra theory, which developed independently in the 1990s–2000s. To my knowledge this link has not been made in the literature.
missed.quote: homomorphisme (algébrique, sans connotations géométriques fixées, pour le moment) de A dans A', est une application f : A → Â' := A' ⊔ {∅} ... X ⊴ Y ⇒ f(X) ⊴ f(Y); X ≪̊ Y ⇒ f(X) ≪̊ f(Y); X|∘|Y ⇒ f(X)|∘|f(Y)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would place Grothendieck's unpublished 'ateliers' (tame-topology era) within mereotopology / de Vries duality. Mostly of historical interest; the content of this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine provisional definition of morphisms (partial relation-preserving maps) with conventions for a null element. It is mildly interesting only as evidence of an unpublished point-free/mereotopological axiomatics ('ateliers') with no published counterpart.
transcription_corrections: The phrase 'toujours vrais' belongs to convention a): 'X' ⊴ ∅, ∅ ⊴ X' toujours vrais'. The same phrase recurs on the next page for c), where the machine reading 'types intégrités' should be 'toujours vrais'.
The condition labels appear to be a), b), c), overwritten from i), ii), iii).
Margin, rotated: likely 'Mais la condition c) cf VIII p. 27 ne veut pas [dire] ...' (partly illegible). It refers to an earlier axiom c).
The second NB reads: 'NB ≪̊ sur Â' est une rel. d'ordre admettant ∅ comme plus petit élt.'
